findings.evidence: Prior independent reviewer reproduced an intermediate polling-lock implementation with no deadline: one stalled fetch prevented subsequent automatic/manual status reads. Current lines 3452-3460 create one AbortController, keep the 10000 ms deadline through r.json(), reject aborted completion and always clear the deadline/release the per-view lock in finally.
findings.impact: A stalled status read could leave payment state unrefreshed while the local countdown continued.
findings.fix: Bound fetch and body read with a request deadline, abort stalled reads, release polling after settlement and reject aborted/obsolete completion.
findings.mitigation: Per-view generation and polling guards; GET-only no-store retries do not submit or retry money actions.
findings.falsePositiveNotes: Finding refers to the prior intermediate implementation; current candidate is fixed. Native body-abort behavior is not independently tested by the VM mock.

reviewObservations.conclusion: Each start increments generation, including same-id reopening. Old poll, body completion, captured open/check functions and timer callbacks cannot apply to a fresh view.

Clearing removes QR src, amount text and requisites contents and disables payment action. Reset runs while card is hidden; new title, instructions, controls, timer and steps are installed before card is revealed.
Polling lock is local to a view. Automatic/manual triggers cannot overlap within that view, including during JSON consumption. Obsolete request settlement cannot unlock the current view.
Status remains the existing authenticated GET with no-store and a 10-second abort deadline. The diff adds no write endpoint, credential source, money authority or automatic financial retry.
Subprocess return code and exact scenario/PASS JSON are both required, preventing unresolved async Node exits from being counted as success.
New route interception holds only same-origin synthetic order GETs. Existing deny-by-default routing, non-root sandbox and simulated/rejected writer/signing boundaries are retained.

newSecuritySinks: No new untrusted-data HTML sink, executable string handler, script loader, storage operation, URL source, auth relaxation or writer introduced. Added steps.innerHTML is a fixed literal. Existing navigation and requisite/tx-link rendering sinks are unchanged and are not certified safe.
conclusion: PASS for this bounded diff/security gate: previous P2 hung-read finding resolved; no new blocking finding. Exact-source 21 payment VM tests, four additional adversarial check groups, parent 97 focused tests and fresh 96-check isolated Chrome evidence pass. Production rollout and whole-stage acceptance remain parent responsibilities.
limits: Bounded four-file diff review, not a whole-application security audit, full E4 closure or production deployment approval.
Existing inline requisites clipboard rendering and transaction-link/navigation sinks are outside this change; no new claim of safety for those unchanged paths.

VM tests use synthetic DOM/timers/fetch; the body-timeout mock explicitly implements signal rejection. Native browser streaming-body timeout and Telegram/iOS/WebKit behavior are not established by those mocks.
One in-flight GET is enforced per displayed view. An obsolete view read may remain until it completes or reaches its deadline; it cannot update the current view.
No backend contract, CSP/edge configuration, SDK, dependency/license audit, customer data, wallet key, credentials, production money action or runtime mutation reviewed or performed.

Browser evidence was executed by parent and inspected by reviewer; screenshots were not visually reviewed here. Native streaming-body timeout, real Telegram, iOS/WebKit, live signing and human comprehension remain unverified.
